title: God Comes to Set Things Right
overview: God answers people who say he ignores injustice by promising to come, purify his people, call them back, and remember those who stayed faithful.

parts.label: A messenger goes ahead (v. 1)
parts.note: This answers people at the end of the previous chapter who asked where God's justice was: God will send a messenger to clear the way, and then the Lord they say they want will suddenly arrive at his temple. The Gospels apply this verse to John the Baptist preparing the way for Jesus, and Christians have read it that way ever since.

parts.label: Fire and soap (vv. 2-5)
parts.note: His coming will be like a metalworker's fire that melts impurities out of silver, or like strong soap scrubbing cloth, starting with the Levites (the tribe who served at the temple) so that worship becomes honest again. The trial also reaches everyday wrongs, such as cheating workers of their pay and denying justice to widows, orphans and foreigners.

parts.label: Still here, so come back (vv. 6-7)
parts.note: The people have survived not because they earned it but because God does not change and keeps his promises to Jacob's family. His offer goes both ways: return to me, and I will return to you.

parts.label: Holding back the tithe (vv. 8-12)
parts.note: The tithe was a tenth of each harvest, brought to temple storerooms to feed the Levites, who had no farmland of their own, and to help the poor, so withholding it is called robbing God. God dares them to bring it all and see whether rain, healthy crops and a good name among the nations do not follow.

parts.label: "Why even bother?" (vv. 13-15)
parts.note: Some people complain that serving God gets them nothing while arrogant, dishonest people thrive and face no consequences. The text treats this as hard talk against God, though the complaint itself is voiced openly and in full.

parts.label: A record of the faithful (vv. 16-18)
parts.note: Those who still honored God talked it over together, and God is pictured listening and having their names written in a scroll of remembrance. A day is promised when he will treat them as his own treasured family, and the difference between those who serve God and those who do not will be plain to see.

disagreement: Christians widely accept the Gospels' link between the messenger and John the Baptist, but they differ on whether the coming Lord's refining judgment points to Jesus's first coming, his future return, or both, and on whether "the Lord" and "the messenger of the covenant" are one figure or two.
think: When people who cut corners seem to do better than those who play fair, what, if anything, keeps someone choosing fairness anyway?
